This appeal is filed by the appellant-accused under Section 14(A)(2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2014 (for short "SC/ST Act") for setting aside the order of dismissal of the bail filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. by the VI Additional District and Special Judge, Mysuru in Spl.C.No.313/2022 dated 19.09.2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 201, 316 of IPC and Section 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act.

sentences.text:
Heard the learned counsel Sri. Parameshwarappa.C for the appellant, learned HCGP Sri. Vishwa Murthy for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel Sri. Jayarama T for respondent No.2.
NC: 2023:KHC:21478 3.
The case of the prosecution as per the de facto complainant is that, her daughter Ashwini was married to the appellant, it was a love marriage and she became 7 months pregnant.

After sometime,
the accused started ill treating her for bringing site or dowry and was harassing her.
There was a panchayat held and advised him to mend his way.
But on 19.03.2022, the deceased did not telephone the complainant.
Therefore, when she tried to contact her daughter through mobile phone, it was switched off.
Hence, she requested her mother to see the deceased in her house.
When her mother went there and checked, she was not found in the house.

Therefore, she contacted one Jayarajeshwari, daughter of her younger sister, to check with the accused about her daughter and then Jayarajeshwari telephoned to the accused and accused informed that deceased went to the hospital.
Subsequently, they could not find the deceased.
Hence, they filed the missing complaint to the police on 19.03.2022 stating that the accused is not giving any proper answer regarding the deceased.
Subsequently, the NC: 2023:KHC:21478 accused was arrested on 21.03.2022 and his voluntary statement was recorded.

It was revealed that on 20.03.2022, the accused committed murder of his wife by smashing/ditching her head to the wall and thereafter, he shifted the dead body in a car and thrown it into melvadi lake and came back.

sentences.text: After recording the voluntary statement, the dead body was recovered at the instance of the accused.
Post -mortem was conducted and he was taken to the custody and remanded to the custody.
The police after investigation filed the charge sheet and his bail application came to be rejected by the Special Judge.
Hence, he is before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent for his alleged offences.
There is no eyewitness to the incident and case is based upon the circumstantial evidence and voluntary statement of the appellant.

Even on perusal of the spot panchanama NC:
2023:KHC:21478 prepared by the police, there is no evidence collected to show that he has smashed the head to the wall and they suspect that the deceased could have administered the poison.
Investigation completed long back and charge sheet has been filed.
He is in custody for more than a year.
He is ready to abide by any of the conditions imposed by this Court.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP along with learned counsel for respondent No.2 submit that the appellant not only committed murder of his wife, but also committed murder of 7 months foetus,
which was in the womb of his wife.
It is nothing but double murder and hence, prays for rejecting the bail.
7. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it was a love marriage between the appellant and the deceased and both of them were of different caste.

Statement of the witnesses reveals that after sometime the appellant started harassing the deceased for dowry or NC:
2023:KHC:21478 to bring the site from her mother.
There was panchayat held in the presence of the witnesses and accused was advised to mend his way.

The accused spotted having intimacy with CW25 and hence, there was quarrel between the husband and wife and during the quarrel, the accused assaulted the deceased by holding her head smashing to the wall and causing death.

Thereafter, he shifted the dead body in the car and thrown it into the belwadi lake and caused disappearance of the evidence and also caused the death of the foetus of 7 months, which was in the deceased's womb.

Of course, the panchanama prepared by the police on the spot, they suspected the accused might have committed murder by using poison, whereas the inquest panchanama and the statement of witnesses on post mortem examination results shows that there was head injury on the head of the deceased and the dead body was thrown to the lake and it was recovered at the instance of the accused on the voluntary statement which is admissible under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Of course, there is no eyewitness.

The house is said to NC: 2023:KHC:21478 have belonged to the relatives of the deceased, but the fact remains that deceased was missing and the accused was with the deceased in the said house and if the wife is dead in the house or elsewhere, it is for the accused to explain what happened to the deceased.

This is exclusive or especial knowledge of the accused under Section 106 of Indian Evidence Act and the dead body was recovered at the instance of the accused and it was found head injury and as per the post mortem report of the Doctor, the head injury could be caused, due to smashing the head to the wall and there was a fracture of skull on the head of the deceased.

8. On perusal of the records, there is a prima facie material placed on record to show that this appellant committed murder of his wife, and the foetus which was in the womb and also destroyed the evidence so as to screen the alleged offences.
Merely, appellant is in custody for one year and Pramod.

The trial court rightly dismissed the application for bail and therefore, there is no requirement of interference of this Court.
Accordingly, appeal is dismissed.
